title: The Erdős similarity conjecture for geometric progressions
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's proof (2026) of the geometric-progression case of the Erdős similarity conjecture: for every q in (0, 1) and every η in (0, 1) there is a compact subset of [0, 1] of measure greater than 1 − η that contains no affine copy x + s{q^n : n ≥ 1}, for any translation x and any nonzero dilation s of either sign. The first lesson introduces measure-universal sets, proves that finite sets are universal, explains why the gap criteria of Falconer, Kolountzakis and Chlebík do not reach geometric progressions, and reduces the theorem to a periodic open hitting set of small density for the dilations between 1 and 2. The second sets up nested dyadic grids with resolution comparable to q^(−b), windows of indices on the edges of a finite ordered tree, stable centers and the separation of the points of one window. The third routes every point through the tree by random selector tables, defines a random set of expected density p, and computes the exact failure probability of the independent tests offered by the first default choice on the route of a center. The fourth controls all dilations at once by finitely many representatives, chooses the parameters, and repairs the remaining centers by a small open set.
prerequisites: core course Measure and Integration (Fremlin, Measure Theory, Volumes 1 and 2): countable additivity and continuity of measures (112C), translation invariance of Lebesgue measure (134A), outer regularity of Lebesgue outer measure (134F(a)), linear changes of variables (263A)
core course Real Analysis I (Lebl, Basic Analysis I): the Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem (Theorem 2.3.8)
finite probability spaces: independence and conditioning on events of positive probability

checks.reading: The manuscript 'The geometric case of the Erdős similarity conjecture' (OpenAI, 5 Oct 2026; main.tex 53 lines, introduction 91, history 71, periodic reduction 74, windows 188, routing 227, scales 194, references.bib; repository folder unchanged at commit 1581d4cb) was read in full on 15 Oct 2026, and every step was derived again while the lessons were written: the reduction to periodic hitting sets with the budgets 4^(−|k|); the dyadic grids N_b, their nesting and the cell width (1 − q)q^b/4; the preorder windows, the spans σ_h and the block bound 2r_h; the density 4Kcq^(g+1) of unstable centers and the preservation of earlier keys; the separation of the points of one window; the random tables and the mean density p; the probability (1 − 2^(1−M))^d of a route without default; the preservation of the route at a stable center; the exact failure probability (1 − p/2)^((M−1)r); the count D_{M,q}(r) of representative dilations; the choice of M, d, g and r_*; the open enlargement, the closed set of missed centers and the repair. No error found. Additions in the course: a proof that finite sets are measure universal from outer regularity alone (no density theorem), the computation that geometric progressions fail Chlebík's hypothesis for all small σ, the exact probability of a route without default as a sum over paths, the closedness of the set of missed centers by the Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem, and the reduction of the conjecture to sequences decreasing to zero (exercise). The companion manuscript 'The dyadic case of the Erdős similarity conjecture' (25 Sep 2026; Lean formalization of its main theorem in the release) has the same architecture for q = 1/2; its section list and the Lean scope note were read, its text was not read line by line. Free sources read on 15 Oct 2026: Chlebík arXiv:1512.05607 (introduction and Theorem 15); Kolountzakis-Papageorgiou arXiv:2208.02637 (introduction, for the history of the problem); the arXiv records of the four other arXiv works in the manuscript's bibliography; Fremlin, Measure Theory, chapters 11 and 13 from the author's site (statements of 112C, 134A, 134F); Lebl, Basic Analysis I, Section 2.3 (numbering of the Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem). Checked by the program plan/checks_20261015/es_check.py (run c passes all 19 tests, output es_check_run_20261015c.txt). Runs a and b failed because of errors in the check program, not in the mathematics: run a computed grid keys in double precision, which cannot separate x from x + t q^n at fine grids, and built the random tables in full (up to 2^64 entries), so the memory watcher stopped it at 7.4 GB; run b used one instance whose stability bound exceeded 1/2, a routing instance whose gap g admitted no stable center, and an overflowing float. The program now uses exact rational arithmetic for all grid computations and generates table entries lazily. Tests: the sum of the measure budgets; Chlebik's hypothesis fails for 15,000 random subsets of G_q; the choice of s_0 in Proposition 1.2; the grid bounds and the nesting of keys; the windows, spans and block bounds for 54 trees and the worked example; the per-window bound 2 N_b' q^(a_e) < 4cq^(g+1) and a sampled density of unstable centers; preservation of earlier keys at stable centers and the separation of one window, exactly; the probability of a route without default (exactly over paths and by sampling) and the mean density p; the preservation of the route and the implication from local tests to membership at 496 stable centers with exact keys; the exact failure probability (1 - p/2)^r by enumeration; the decay of D_{M,q}(r) e^(-alpha r); the worked parameters M = 29 and d = 618,095,479; the count of lattice points met by x + t q^n.
